'''Lyle Vincent Jones''' (March 11, 1924 – April 13, 2016) was an American psychologist known for his pioneering work in [[psychometrics]]. He was an early architect of the [[National Assessment of Educational Progress]].<ref name=observer/>

==Early life and education==
Jones was born in [[Grandview, Washington]] on March 11, 1924. He began taking classes at [[Reed College]] in 1942. A year later, immediately after completing his freshman year, he left Reed to begin active duty in the [[United States Army Air Corps]].<ref name=observer>{{Cite news |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/community/chapel-hill-news/chn-obituaries/article74987702.html |title=Lyle Vincent Jones |date=2016-05-03 |work=News & Observer |access-date=2018-01-19 |language=en}}</ref> He continued to serve in the Air Corps until 1946, when he attended the [[University of Washington]] to complete his bachelor's degree. He then received his master's degree, also from the University of Washington, before receiving his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1950.<ref name=jebs>{{Cite journal |date=2003-12-01 |title=Lyle V. Jones: Biography |journal=Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics |volume=28 |issue=4 |pages=389–394 |doi=10.3102/10769986028004389|s2cid=220337995 }}</ref>

==Career==
After receiving his Ph.D., Jones began teaching at the [[University of Chicago]] and the [[University of Texas]] before joining the faculty of the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] (UNC-Chapel Hill) in 1957.<ref name=reed>{{Cite web |url=http://www.reed.edu/reed-magazine/in-memoriam/obituaries/september2016/lyle-vincent-jones-1944.html |title=Lyle Vincent Jones '44 |last=College |first=Reed |date=September 2016 |website=Reed Magazine  |language=en-us |access-date=2018-01-19}}</ref> At UNC-Chapel Hill, he worked with [[Louis Leon Thurstone]] at the Psychometric Laboratory (later renamed the L. L. Thurstone Psychometric Laboratory). Jones served as director of the Psychometric Laboratory from 1957 until he retired in 1992, except for a five-year hiatus.<ref name=psychometrika>{{Cite journal |last=Thissen |first=David |date=2016-07-07 |title=Remembering Lyle V. Jones (1924–2016) |url=https://www.deepdyve.com/lp/springer-journals/remembering-lyle-v-jones-1924-2016-B1IjHvKXCu |journal=Psychometrika |language=en |volume=81 |issue=3 |pages=904–905 |doi=10.1007/s11336-016-9510-4 |pmid=27388290 |s2cid=37772324 |issn=0033-3123}}</ref> For ten years (1969–79), he was also vice chancellor at UNC-Chapel Hill and dean of the graduate school there.<ref name=reed/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://museum.unc.edu/exhibits/show/faculty/lyle-v--jones--1924--- |title=Lyle V. Jones (1924- )  |website=Carolina Story: Virtual Museum of University History |language=en-US |access-date=2018-01-19}}</ref> Beginning in 1992, he was a research professor at UNC-Chapel Hill.<ref name=jebs/>

===Other positions===
Jones was the managing editor of ''[[Psychometrika]]'' from 1956 to 1961, the president of the [[Psychometric Society]] from 1962 to 1963, and president of the [[American Psychological Association]]'s Division 5 from 1963 to 1964.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://psychology.unc.edu/2016/08/23/remembered-dr-lyle-v-jones-1924-2016/ |title=Remembered: Dr. Lyle V. Jones, 1924-2016 |date=2016-08-23 |website=Department Of Psychology and Neuroscience |language=en-US |access-date=2018-01-19}}</ref>

==Death and recognition==
Jones died on April 13, 2016, in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], at the age of 92.<ref name=psychometrika/> In his honor, UNC-Chapel Hill established the Lyle V. Jones Award, which it awards every year to a graduate student in the L. L. Thurstone Psychometric Laboratory "who epitomizes both academic excellence and community engagement within the lab."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://psychology.unc.edu/2016/11/22/veronica-cole-selected-for-2016-lyle-v-jones-award/ |title=Veronica Cole Selected for 2016 Lyle V. Jones Award  |date=2016-11-22 |website=Department Of Psychology and Neuroscience |language=en-US |access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref>
